Weather on I dag

Issue #433 · design run 1 · unattended, one direction

Chosen: Stille kolonne, with 5 build changes run 1 8 decisions all two-way doors

Comparison

Stille kolonne
Place on the axisMiddle of density: a fixed fourth column on each day’s first row; not folded into the facts line, not a band of its own
GainSeven days read down one edge: you scan the column and see the dry day without reading any titles
Cost3.5rem out of every titled row: at 390px a title gets about 150px before it wraps
Criteria held9 of 12 hold; AC 7 partly (the card’s weather is silent to a screen reader); AC 12 partly (only the in-page line is drawn); AC 11 is server work with nothing to draw
Worst caseAt 390px the column holds −23°, 12,4 mm and three-line titles. Below about 345px at 100% text, long titles break inside words (Terskelinterv-aller), which today’s rows never do; free days’ weather sits 8px off the column’s edge
Build costNot rated: one variant, so the build-cost part does not run
StatusChosen

Decisions

  • Where does a day’s weather sit? In its own right-hand column, before the mark, on the day’s first row only. Today’s row has none, since the card shows it.
  • How does the card show it? As one line under the sentence: glyph, the word (Lett regn) over the hour, and the temperature over the rain.
  • Which symbols? The app’s monochrome Tabler sprite, mapped from MET’s symbol families (7 glyphs, night variants included), with one Hugeicons glyph for partly cloudy. Not MET’s colour icon set.
  • Where is the home place set? On a row in Meg › Innstillinger that opens its own page, Hjemsted. Picking a place saves it straight away; Fjern removes it with no confirmation.
  • How are the numbers written? 6° and −23° with a true minus sign; rain to one decimal with a comma, and 0 mm when dry. The screen reader hears “grader” and “millimeter nedbør”.
  • Where is MET credited? Once, under the week list, whenever any weather shows.
  • Does weather move? No. It is seen every day and never changes in place, so nothing animates.
  • What must the build change from the prototype? (1) Speak the card’s weather with visually hidden text, not aria-label on a paragraph; (2) with a place set, stack the weather into the day line below a 20rem row, so titles never break inside a word; (3) give the last column one fixed width so the weather keeps one edge on free days; (4) let a row with no weather (past, today, beyond the forecast) give its empty 3.5rem to the title; (5) show a municipality match as Kommune · Troms, not its name twice.

Fit: it lives inside the calm view’s own row and card (ADR 0101) and adds one Meg row in the existing list pattern; the search should be built on the existing command.tsx/input-group.tsx primitives with filtering off. The day-level weather is the unit weather-aware Bytt dag will need next, and the column has room for one more glyph (a warning) but not for a second value; anything more belongs in the detail, not the row.

Build cost: not rated (one variant, no build-cost part).

Designer’s disagreement

None: the designer’s sealed pick is also Stille kolonne.

Method

The tool was Emil’s prototype, standalone branch: one self-contained HTML file (stille-kolonne.html) in the project’s tokens, copied from app/styles/tailwind.css. Its markup and grid mirror app/routes/_home/__calm-today-view.tsx (the row is 2.75rem minmax(0,1fr) auto, which becomes 2.75rem minmax(0,1fr) 3.5rem auto once a place is set) and app/routes/me.tsx. The prototype-ui skill folder is not installed in this environment, so its standalone shape was followed from the task’s description of it, under emil-design-eng, mobile-native and break-ui.

Settled by probe: does a fourth column fit? Playwright measured horizontal overflow in every state. It was 0px at 390px and at 1440px. At 320px with 200% text it was 9px, which went to 0 once the weather joins the stacked day line and the card’s line stacks.

Driven in the browser: typing “Vik” gave 6 matches; arrow keys and Enter picked Vik, Sømna, Nordland and saved it; a search with no match kept the text and said so; Fjern cleared the place. Without a place, I dag has no weather cell, no credit and the old three-column grid. No page errors.

break-ui findings

  • On a wrap, the card’s hour was left alone on its own line. Fixed by laying the card line out as a grid (word over hour).
  • In the stacked layout (narrow rows), the empty weather cell pushed the mark onto a new line. Fixed: an empty cell hides with the column.
  • 1 mm sat beside 12,4 mm. Fixed: rain always has one decimal unless it is 0.
  • When the place is itself the municipality, the name shows twice (Kommune · Gáivuotna – Kåfjord – Kaivuono, Troms). Left as it is so AC 1 holds literally. The builder may shorten it to Kommune i Troms.
  • At 320px with 200% text, long words break inside the card (this happens on today’s card too). Nothing here makes it worse.

review-animations

BeforeAfterWhy
(new) weather valuesno motionSeen daily and static: the frequency rule says no animation
(new) search resultsno motion; option press is a tint, 160ms --ease-outResults follow each keystroke. A list row tints rather than scales, as MeLink does
(new) Fjern, backpressableThe system’s press

Verdict: pass, with no Block.

mobile-native: every target is at least 44px (rows 56px, input 44px, options 56px). The input is 16px, type=search with enterkeyhint=search. Hover is gated to fine pointers. Still needs a real phone: whether the keyboard covers the results under interactive-widget=resizes-content, how the debounce feels, and whether 16px glyphs read in daylight.

Notes for the build

  • Beyond about 60 hours, MET compact gives 6-hourly steps. A day’s value is the step that covers its hour, so the hour shown is the one asked for.
  • At 07:00 in November it is dark, so *_night symbols map to the moon glyph.
  • The dashed outline on the Meg row only marks what is new in the prototype. It is not part of the design.

Rejected directions

  • Weather in the facts line (1 t · hard · 6° 0,6 mm): no column to scan, and on a free day there are no facts to sit beside.
  • A weather band under each day: twice the height of the week for an aid.
  • MET’s colour icons: loud next to the calm I dag, and a second icon system beside the sprite.
  • The search inline in Meg or in the Utøverprofil form: a results list inside a long page or a form with a save button fights both.

Stille kolonne Chosen

Working prototype. Use its bar at the bottom of each frame to switch between I dag, Meg and Hjemsted, with or without a place, light or dark, and 100% or 200% text.

Held up: −35° and 28,6 mm fit 3.5rem (56px, at its limit); dark glyphs read in the foreground colour; no horizontal scroll at any width; 200% text stacks cleanly; nine places called Vik are told apart.

These are thunder showers on a free day at 21:00, −23° under heavy snow, sleet with thunder on a free day, a day with three sessions, a day beyond the forecast (Sunday, which shows nothing), a long plan name, nine places called Vik, and a three-language municipality name.
